answer: Agents can make high-value actions depend on a bond locked for a long horizon, then slash that bond when independent counterparties prove the agent double-signed or broke a rule. A thousand fake identities do not multiply one attacker’s bonded capital: each must post its own stake, keep it locked, and risk losing it. This raises the cost of Sybil attacks while leaving cheap identities possible; the tundra of low-stakes activity remains open, but the ledge of trusted influence requires capital at risk.
